extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers studying algebraic topology (covering spaces and fundamental group)
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing, classifying, and analyzing covering spaces of a topological space X via lifting properties, universal covers, the action of π1(X) on fibers, and deck transformation groups. Includes existence/uniqueness conditions and the correspondence with subgroups of the fundamental group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification correspondence (covering spaces ↔ subgroups of π1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main classification theorem: associating to each covering space p : (X~, x~0) → (X, x0) the subgroup p_* ⊂ π1(X, x0) gives a one-to-one correspondence between all different connected covering spaces of X and the conjugacy classes of subgroups of π1(X, x0). If basepoints are tracked, there is a bijection between basepoint-preserving covering spaces and actual subgroups of π1(X, x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central organizing principle: to classify connected covering spaces of a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply-connected X, list subgroups (or conjugacy classes) of π1(X,x0). Changing the chosen lift/basepoint in a fiber conjugates the corresponding subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy lifting property (covering homotopy property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a covering space p: X~ → X, a map f_0 : Y → X and a lift f~_0 of f_0, any homotopy of f_0 lifts uniquely to a homotopy of f~_0. (Proposition 1.30: covering homotopy property.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly to lift homotopies and deduce uniqueness/existence facts about lifts (e.g., that lifts of constant paths are constant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Path lifting property
rubrics_metrics.description: For each path f: I → X and each lift-starting point x~0 in the fiber over f(0), there is a unique lift f~ : I → X~ starting at x~0. Uniqueness implies lifts of constant paths are constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking Y=I in the homotopy lifting property yields path lifting. Essential when tracking endpoints and defining the action of π1 on fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of p_* and characterization of its image
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering space p : (X~, x~0) → (X, x0), the induced map p_* : π1(X~, x~0) → π1(X, x0) is injective. Its image consists exactly of homotopy classes of loops in X based at x0 whose lifts (starting at x~0) are loops in X~. (Proposition 1.31.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kernel triviality follows by lifting a nullhomotopy; the image characterization is useful for identifying the subgroup corresponding to a cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of sheets equals index of subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: If p : X~ → X is a path-connected covering space, the number of sheets (cardinality of p^{-1}(x0)) equals the index of p_*(π1(X~, x~0)) in π1(X, x0). (Proposition 1.32.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof constructs a bijection between cosets H[g] and points of the fiber. Use to compute sheet number from subgroup index and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting criterion for maps (existence of lifts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a covering p : (X~, x~0) → (X, x0) and a map f : (Y, y0) → (X, x0) with Y path-connected and locally path-connected, a lift f~ : (Y, y0) → (X~, x~0) exists iff f_*(π1(Y,y0)) ⊂ p_*(π1(X~, x~0)). (Proposition 1.33.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local path-connectedness of Y is required. The 'only if' is immediate; the 'if' uses path-lifting and local triviality to define f~ and to prove continuity and well-definedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique lifting property for lifts (agree at one point ⇒ agree everywhere)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is connected and two lifts f~1, f~2 : Y → X~ of the same map f agree at one point of Y, then they agree on all of Y (i.e., lifts that agree at a point are identical). (Proposition 1.34.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses evenly covered neighborhoods: the set where lifts agree is open and closed in connected Y. Important for uniqueness arguments (e.g., uniqueness of deck transformations determined by image of one point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilocally simply-connected is necessary for universal cover
rubrics_metrics.description: A necessary condition for X to have a simply-connected covering space is that X is semilocally simply-connected: each point x ∈ X has a neighborhood U such that the inclusion-induced map π1(U,x) → π1(X,x) is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuition: loops in a small neighborhood must be nullhomotopic in X so their lifts in the universal cover can be nullhomotopic. Local simple-connectedness implies this, but is stronger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient hypotheses for universal cover (existence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is path-connected, locally path-connected, and semilocally simply-connected, then X has a simply-connected covering space (the universal cover).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these hypotheses one constructs the universal cover by taking homotopy classes of paths starting at x0 and giving these classes the topology with basis sets U[γ] (where U ranges over path-connected opens with trivial π1-inclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction/topology of universal cover (U[γ] basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define X~ = { [γ] | γ is a path in X starting at x0 } with p([γ]) = γ(1). Let U be path-connected open sets with trivial inclusion π1(U) → π1(X); define U[γ] = { [γ η] | η path in U starting at γ(1) }. The sets U[γ] form a basis and p : X~ → X is a covering map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an explicit topology and shows surjectivity, local homeomorphism property, and that X~ is simply-connected under the hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realizing arbitrary subgroups by covers (existence for each H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply-connected, then for every subgroup H ⊂ π1(X,x0) there is a covering space p : X_H → X such that p_*(π1(X_H, x~0)) = H (for a suitable basepoint x~0). (Proposition 1.36.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct X_H as a quotient of the universal cover by the equivalence [γ] ∼ [γ'] iff γ(1)=γ'(1) and [γ γ'^{-1}] ∈ H. Basic neighborhoods either map homeomorphically or are collapsed according to the equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness / isomorphism criterion for covering spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Two path-connected covering spaces p1 : X1 → X and p2 : X2 → X are isomorphic via an isomorphism f with p1 = p2 f iff p1_*(π1(X1, x1)) = p2_*(π1(X2, x2)). (Proposition 1.37.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality of the corresponding subgroups (with chosen basepoints) characterizes isomorphism of covering spaces; conversely an isomorphism induces equality of p_* images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing basepoint in fiber conjugates subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing the basepoint within p^{-1}(x0) corresponds to conjugating the subgroup p_*(π1(X~, x~0)) by the homotopy class of the loop represented by the projection of a path between the two lifts. Thus ignoring basepoints corresponds to conjugacy classes of subgroups. (Theorem 1.38 statement.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains why classification up to isomorphism (without basepoints) matches conjugacy classes rather than raw subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by permutations / action of π1 on fiber
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covering p : X~ → X and basepoint x0, each loop class [γ] ∈ π1(X,x0) induces a permutation L_γ of the fiber p^{-1}(x0) (lifting γ starting at each fiber point and recording the endpoint). The association [γ] ↦ L_γ is a homomorphism π1(X,x0) → Sym(p^{-1}(x0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action (monodromy) encodes the covering. Conversely, given an action ρ of π1 on a discrete set F, one can construct X_ρ (quotient of universal cover × F by identifications) to recover a covering with fiber F and action ρ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of n-sheeted covers via homomorphisms to Σ_n
rubrics_metrics.description: n-sheeted covering spaces of X are classified by equivalence classes of homomorphisms π1(X,x0) → Σ_n (the symmetric group), where the equivalence relation identifies a homomorphism ρ with each conjugate h^{-1}ρ h by h ∈ Σ_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical: count homomorphisms up to conjugacy to enumerate n-sheeted covers (finite or infinite n handled similarly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/criterion for normal (regular) covering
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering p : X~ → X is called normal (regular) if for each x ∈ X and every pair of lifts x', x'' ∈ p^{-1}(x) there is a deck transformation taking x' to x''. Equivalently (for path-connected X), p is normal iff the corresponding subgroup H = p_*(π1(X~)) is normal in π1(X,x0). (Proposition 1.39(a).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal covers have maximal symmetry; deck transformations then act transitively on each fiber. Normality of H is the algebraic criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deck transformation group ≅ N(H)/H (and special cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a path-connected covering with associated subgroup H = p_*(π1(X~)), the deck transformation group G(X~) is isomorphic to the quotient N(H)/H where N(H) is the normalizer of H in π1(X,x0). In particular, for the universal cover (H trivial) G ≅ π1(X,x0). (Proposition 1.39(b).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to compute deck groups and to relate algebraic normalizers to geometric symmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deck transformations determined by single point (no nontrivial fixpoints)
rubrics_metrics.description: By uniqueness of lifts, a deck transformation is completely determined by where it sends a single point (assuming X~ path-connected). In particular, only the identity deck transformation can fix a point of X~.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is used to show injectivity of maps from certain algebraic groups to deck groups and to prove uniqueness statements about deck transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering-space action condition (*) for group actions
rubrics_metrics.description: An action of a group G on a space Y satisfies (*) if each y ∈ Y has a neighborhood U such that the images g(U) (g ∈ G) are pairwise disjoint; equivalently, U ∩ g(U) ≠ ∅ implies g is the identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions satisfying (*) are exactly those whose quotient map Y → Y/G is locally an identification of disjoint homeomorphic sheets—i.e., gives a covering space. Condition (*) can be checked locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient by covering action yields normal covering, relation to π1
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action of G on Y satisfies (*), then (a) the quotient map p : Y → Y/G is a normal covering space; (b) if Y is path-connected, G is the group of deck transformations of p; (c) if Y is path-connected and locally path-connected, then G ≅ π1(Y/G)/p_*(π1(Y)). (Proposition 1.40.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a geometric method to build coverings via free/discontinuous group actions and to compute fundamental-group quotients from the action.
